title: Crypto-audit tokenization and cross-tenant redaction policy
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
This document describes Redwoods standard for cryptographic audit tokenization, multi-tenant redaction, and how tokenized audit streams are retained and packaged as compliance evidence. It defines architecture, event schema extensions, key management requirements, verification procedures for auditors and incident responders, and a risk/exception handling process.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Reduce exposure of tenant-sensitive identifiers and PII in our long-term audit archive while preserving cryptographic proof-of-origin and the ability to rehydrate evidence for authorized investigation and audits.
- Scope: Applies to all production services that emit audit events into Redwoods centralized audit pipeline (audit-edge, ingestion, streaming, and cold-tier storage). Covers events for authentication/authorization (RBAC), model-serving inference logs, billing-relevant metadata, and administrative actions.
- Exclusions: Ephemeral debug logs (non-audit debug) and internal engineering sandboxes that do not feed the centralized audit pipeline.

Guiding principles
1) Minimally sufficient fidelity: Audit events retain schema fields required for reconstruction of a sequence-of-actions (timestamps, action type, resource type, outcome) while sensitive identifiers are replaced by verifiable tokens.
2) Verifiability: Tokens are cryptographically bound to the original identifier and to an event digest so investigators can cryptographically prove lineage without exposing the identifier in normal query flows.
3) Tenant separation and least privilege: Cross-tenant queries and support access must never return raw tenant identifiers unless an access workflow with attestation and approval is followed.
4) Retention and rehydration controls: Rehydration (revealing original identifiers) requires multi-party approval, timeboxed keys, and an audited packaging step that generates evidence bundles.

Architecture overview
- Producers: Application services produce canonical audit events (JSON) with a clear audit schema (see section Event schema). Producers call the Tokenization Service before emitting to the centralized stream.
- Tokenization Service (stateless API + HSM-backed signing): Replaces sensitive fields with a token and returns a signed token object containing a token_id, token_type, signer_id, and a signature over (tenant_id || original_value_hash || event_digest || timestamp).
- Audit Stream (Kafka): Tokenized events flow to the streaming tier. Consumers (alerting, SLO calculators, forensic indexing) operate on tokenized values.
- Key Management: Signing keys are held in KMS/HSM and rotated per policy. A separate rehydration keyset (limited-wrapping-keys) is required to unwrap confidential values and is controlled by the Evidence Service.
- Evidence Service: Orchestrates rehydration requests, approval workflows, transient key material creation, evidence packaging (signed bundle + index), and audit trail recording.

Event schema (required fields and tokenized patterns)
- Common top-level fields: event_id, timestamp, service, environment, severity, action, status, context
- Sensitive fields that must be tokenized at ingestion: user_id, account_id, api_key_id, session_id, model_input/embedding_id when it maps to PII, storage_object_path when it references customer-provided data
- Token object (example inserted in event):
  "tokenized_fields": [{
    "field_path": "context.user_id",
    "token": "TKN_7b3f...",
    "token_type": "sha256-hmac+sign",
    "signer": "token-svc-v2",
    "signature": "base64(sig)",
    "hash_alg": "sha256"
  }]
- The original hashed value is never stored in plain text in the stream. Instead, the token payload contains a hash of the original value (salted with tenant_id) that is part of the signature input so verification is possible without revealing the original.

Tokenization workflow (producer perspective)
1) Producer computes value_hash = HMAC(salt = tenant_id, value = original_identifier) using local service salt (rotated weekly).
2) Producer calls Tokenization Service: POST /tokenize { "tenant_id", "field_path", "value_hash", "event_digest" }
3) Tokenization Service issues token_id and signs (tenant_id || value_hash || event_digest || issued_at) with the HSM private key.
4) Producer writes the event replacing original_identifier with token_id and attaching the token metadata.
5) Central consumers treat token_id as opaque; only Evidence Service can request rehydration.

Key management and rotation
- Signing keys: Stored in KMS with HSM wrapping. Keys are rotated every 365 days, with an overlap window of 7 days for verification compatibility.
- Salt material: Service-level salts used to compute value_hash are rotated weekly. Salt rotations are logged and recorded in the salt registry.
- Rehydration keys: Strictly restricted. Rehydration requires a tombstone key that is created transiently, wrapped to the Evidence Service, and destroyed after bundle generation.
- Compromise procedure: If a signing key is suspected compromised, immediately stop acceptance of token signatures, issue a token revocation snapshot, and consult the Evidence and Legal teams for containment.

Rehydration and evidence packaging process
- Authorization gates: Rehydration requires: (a) at least two approvers from distinct teams (security and legal or security and customer-success), (b) a documented justification, (c) an expiration time for the rehydration session, and (d) an integrity check via event_digest verification.
- Packaging steps (automated by Evidence Service):
  1) Validate approvals and attestations.
  2) Create transient rehydration key bound to the request (TTL configurable, default 4 hours).
  3) Recompute value_hash for candidate tokens and attempt one-way mapping to original values stored in the Protected Mapping Store (PMS) accessible only to Evidence Service.
  4) Generate evidence bundle: zipped directory containing (i) tokenized event slice, (ii) rehydrated field mapping, (iii) signature chain and timestamp, (iv) approver audit trail, (v) integrity manifest (SHA256 checksums).
  5) Digitally sign the evidence bundle with Evidence Service signing key and store the bundle in restricted cold storage with a recorded access policy.
- Evidence delivery: Bundles for external auditors are delivered via an encrypted transfer channel (SFTP over VPN or customer-managed bucket with pre-signed URL + IP restrictions) and logged.

Operational runbook: investigating an RBAC anomaly with tokenized logs
1) Trigger: Alert from SSO or abnormal access pattern with referenced token IDs.
2) Triage: Determine tenant_id and affected token_ids from tokenized events.
3) Request rehydration: Open Evidence Service request (link generated automatically), include justification, and tag legal/security approvers.
4) Approvers review: Approvals must include an explicit timebox and expected recipients of the bundle.
5) Evidence Service packages bundle and posts an immutable record to the incident ticket.
6) Investigator receives bundle and performs correlation; any further rehydration requests for the same incident require a new approval.
7) Post-incident: Evidence expiration and deletion policy enforced; a retention snapshot is recorded for compliance tracing.

Retention, archival tiers, and deletion
- Hot tier (90 days): searchable tokenized stream stored in primary cluster.
- Warm tier (1 year): compacted tokenized events with indexed metadata.
- Cold tier (7 years default for regulated customers): tokenized events and signed evidence bundles (not plain identifiers).
- Rehydrated bundles persisted only if explicitly required by legal/regulatory hold; otherwise bundles are deleted after TTL and deletion is recorded and attested.

Audit and monitoring requirements
- SLOs: Tokenization latency must be < 20 ms p95 for 99% of requests; tokenization service errors must be < 0.1% monthly.
- Telemetry: Token issuance (count, latency), token verification attempts, rehydration requests (approvals, denials), key rotation events, and evidence bundle generation are emitted to security telemetry.
- Alerts: Tokenization service error spike, Evidence Service approval delays > 8 hours for high-severity incidents, key rotation failure.

Verification for auditors (ad-hoc)
- Auditor verification flow (read-only):
  1) Auditor receives signed evidence bundle and the Evidence Service public verification key.
  2) Auditor validates the evidence bundle signature and checks the manifest checksums.
  3) Auditor verifies token signatures against the token-svc public key and validates that token hashes correspond to tenant-provided sample identifiers (if permitted by NDA).
  4) For deeper verification, Redwood can perform a controlled rehydration in the presence of auditors following the standard approval gates.

Risk and exception handling
- Acceptable risks: Tokenization may reduce immediate readability for on-call engineers; mitigated by fast rehydration workflows and a rich token-to-metadata index for common diagnostics.
- Exceptions: Short-lived exceptions (e.g., emergency platform-wide debugging) may allow temporarily retaining un-tokenized fields, but must be recorded in the Exception Register with: owner, justification, TTL, and compensating controls (access logging, IP restrictions).
- Exception approval flow: Team Lead -> Security -> Legal (for cross-border data). Exceptions are timeboxed and audited.

Ownership and roles
- Tokenization Service: eng-infra (owner), oncall: infra-audits@redwood.com
- Evidence Service: security (owner), oncall: sec-evidence@redwood.com
- Key management & rotation: cloud-security team (owner), oncall: kms-ops@redwood.com
- Compliance packaging & external delivery: customer-success + security (shared)

Appendix A: Example tokenization request (producer)
POST /tokenize HTTP/1.1
Host: token-svc.internal.redwood.com
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp-123",
  "field_path": "context.user_id",
  "value_hash": "hmac-sha256:4f2b...",
  "event_digest": "sha256:ab12..."
}

Example token object returned:
{
  "token_id": "TKN_7b3f4c8a",
  "signer": "token-svc-v2",
  "signature": "base64(...)",
  "issued_at": "2026-03-15T18:22:31Z",
  "token_type": "sha256-hmac+sign",
  "hash_alg": "sha256"
}

Appendix B: Evidence bundle manifest (excerpt)
- bundle_id: EVID_20260315_0009
- requestor: sec-ops
- approvers: [security@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com]
- token_count: 42
- signed_by: evidence-svc-key-v1
- checksums: { "events.json": "sha256:...", "mapping.csv": "sha256:..." }

Policy change log
- 2026-03-15: Initial published policy and architecture (Maya Chen).
- 2026-06-02: Clarified rehydration TTLs and added SLOs for tokenization service (Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-09-02: Added cross-tenant redaction clarifications and tightened rehydration approval requirements (Priya Nair).
